title: 2003 AMC 10B Problem 7
statement: The symbolism \(\lfloor x \rfloor\) denotes the largest integer not exceeding \(x.\) For example, \(\lfloor 3 \rfloor = 3,\) and \(\lfloor \frac{9}{2} \rfloor = 4.\) Compute \[ \begin{gathered} \lfloor \sqrt{1} \rfloor + \lfloor \sqrt{2} \rfloor + \lfloor \sqrt{3} \rfloor \\ {}+ \cdots + \lfloor \sqrt{16} \rfloor. \end{gathered} \]

solutions.text:
The value is \(1\) for \(n=1,2,3;\) it is \(2\) for \(n=4,\ldots,8;\) it is \(3\) for \(n=9,\ldots,15;\) and it is \(4\) for \(n=16.\) The sum is \[3\cdot 1 + 5\cdot 2 + 7\cdot 3 + 1\cdot 4 = 38.\]

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Count how many of \(1\) through \(16\) give each floor value \(1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) and \(4\)
